sections.heading: Are There Any Working Break and Steal an Egg Codes?
paragraphs: The current confirmed working code count is zero. There is no string on this page to copy, and no confirmed code reward to claim. If you came here looking for Break and Steal an Egg codes for October 2026, that is the answer before you spend time testing lists from other games.

A code normally means an actual redeemable text string, together with a way for the correct game to accept it. A reward announcement alone does not provide either of those things. The absence of confirmed codes also does not tell us whether the developer will add them later. Treat today's status as a dated answer, rather than a promise about every future update.

sections.heading: Codes vs. Community Rewards
paragraphs: The official Roblox listing encourages players to like the game and join its group for free rewards. That is a community reward offer. It does not establish a redeem code, a code redemption menu, or a particular reward amount. Follow the instructions the game itself displays for that offer instead of typing the words “Like” or the group name into an imagined code field.

This distinction matters when comparing Break and Steal an Egg code lists. A page may discuss a real free reward while presenting it as if there were a working code. Look for the actual string and the correct experience before treating the claim as redeemable. Animal names, promotional phrases and group names are not confirmed codes just because they appear near an offer.

No specific community reward item, quantity or collection button is listed here. The official description confirms the offer at a high level; the current game is the place to check its details. You can still use the ordinary earning loop without waiting for a code announcement.

sections.heading: How We Handle New Codes
paragraphs: New codes will be listed when an actual redeemable string for this ILGames x Eggs experience, its reward and its current working status are confirmed. Instructions will describe the redemption method shown in the game or announced by the developer. An expiry date will only be listed if it has been announced.

For now, there is no confirmed redemption walkthrough. We cannot name a button, describe a menu location or tell you to enter a string into a field that has not been established. If codes are introduced, the answer at the top of this page should change alongside the usable details, so you can see the current status immediately.

Check the last updated date when returning after an update. A page dated October 8 describes that day's code status; an event scheduled for October 11 is not itself proof that codes will be released. New areas and redeem codes are different kinds of news.

sections.heading: Avoid Codes From the Wrong Egg Game
paragraphs: Break and Steal an Egg is the ILGames x Eggs Roblox experience with Place ID 114326934417838 and Universe ID 10765288803. Steal An Egg is a different experience. Similar titles and egg artwork can make search results look interchangeable, but a code associated with another game is not a confirmed code for this one.

Use the official game link to check the destination, then compare the developer and Place ID. Do this before following a guide that promises free animals or Cash. Matching only the words “egg” or “steal” is too broad: this wiki covers the game where you break eggs, take the animals, escape guards and bring them back to your base.

This page does not maintain an expired list filled with strings from unrelated games. Without an established code for this experience, calling it expired would be just as misleading as calling it active. The current answer stays focused on confirmed working codes.

sections.heading: What to Do While There Are No Codes
paragraphs: You can progress through the official gameplay loop while the code count is zero. Break an egg in a zone you can reach, take the animal that hatches, return past the guards and place it at your base to earn Cash. For a new player, learning that full route is more useful than repeatedly trying unconfirmed strings.

Next, identify the part of a run that slows you down. Pickaxe Power helps with breaking eggs. Speed helps with movement and zone progression, while an equipped Trail provides its Speed multiplier. A bigger satchel lets you carry more animals per run. These systems address different problems, so choose your next upgrade around what you actually need.

Use the guides below to make a practical next step. The beginner guide explains the first return to base; the zone guide lists current Speed gates. Neither requires a code reward to understand. You can also return to the main wiki for the current overview and official Roblox link.

sections.heading: What Is Confirmed About the New Biome

It does not, by itself, explain whether the area will remain available after the window ends or whether any part of the update is time limited. No separate access deadline or reward expiry has been announced in the information available for this guide.

The event is titled NEW BIOME 🪲. Its announcement says a new area is coming to Break and Steal an Egg. Together with the scheduled start and end times, those are the details you can use now without guessing how the area will work.

The title's beetle emoji is part of the event name. It is not enough to establish a particular egg, animal, boss or reward. Likewise, “new area” does not specify where the area sits in the current progression or how players will enter it. Keep the announced wording separate from ideas about what might appear.

The developer of the game is ILGames x Eggs. This fan-made wiki is a guide to the announcement, not the organizer of the Roblox event. Use the official game page as your destination when the scheduled window opens, especially if a search result takes you to a similarly named egg game.

Review your equipment as well as your purchases. Trails need to be equipped for their multiplier to apply. Pickaxes provide Power for breaking eggs, while zone gates use Speed. Understanding that split helps you avoid spending Cash on a tool when your actual difficulty is reaching a zone.

Keeping some progression resources available is a flexible choice, but there is no announced amount to save. Continue the parts of the game you enjoy and use your actual bottleneck to decide purchases. Preparation does not require rushing to Galaxy or buying a specific late-game item.

When the window starts, reopen the official Roblox page and read the current description and any instructions shown in the game. Look for the name, access condition and available eggs before deciding what to upgrade. A useful launch plan starts with the new information, not with a requirement guessed days earlier.

sections.heading: How Zone Speed Requirements Work
paragraphs: Use this table to find your next zone, then check its eggs and rarity. This guide was updated October 8, 2026 using the current nine-zone progression reference. Full numbers make the differences between gates visible: Galaxy's 25B means 25,000,000,000 Speed, not a Cash price or a Pickaxe Power value.

The route runs Forest, Desert, Snowy, Candy, Swamp, Ocean, Hell, Blossom and Galaxy. A higher entry in the table gives you a progression target, but it does not tell you how comfortable the full run will be. You still need to break an egg, take its animal and return to base past the guards.

Speed is the stat to compare with the zone gate. Cash is what you earn from animals placed at your base and use for purchases; it is not the number in the Speed column. Pickaxe Power affects egg breaking. Even a strong tool does not substitute for the required Speed.

Trails belong to Speed progression and must be equipped to apply their multiplier. A particular Trail is not a guaranteed ticket to a particular zone, because players start from different actual Speed values. Check your own Speed after setting up equipment instead of deciding from the Trail name alone.

Once a zone is reachable, judge it through a complete run. Entry, egg breaking and the return to your base are separate parts of the loop. If only one part causes difficulty, an upgrade aimed at a different part may leave the problem unresolved.

subsections.heading: Forest
paragraphs: Forest is the first entry at 5 Speed. Its Rock Egg and Forest Egg sit in the Common rarity tier. Use this opening area to learn a full return: break an egg, take the hatched animal, get away from the guards and place it at your base. The point of an early run is to understand all of those actions, rather than only breaking the first egg. Check your current Speed against the next gate before moving on, and use what slowed the run to choose an upgrade.

subsections.heading: Desert
paragraphs: Desert follows at 1,000 Speed, with Cactus Egg and Bones Egg in the Uncommon tier. This is your next reference after Forest, but the gate is a Speed target, not a recommendation to buy a particular Pickaxe. Before planning a Desert run, compare your actual stat with the table. Once entry is possible, look separately at how quickly you can break its eggs and how well you can bring an animal back. Those observations tell you more about the next useful purchase than the zone name does.

subsections.heading: Snowy
paragraphs: Snowy requires 50,000 Speed and lists Frozen Egg and Yeti Egg at Rare rarity. It closes the early group in this guide. The increase from Desert is substantial, so read the complete number rather than confusing 50K Speed with an equipment cost. Being able to enter is the first check; breaking and returning remain important afterward. If progress slows here, separate the access question from the egg-breaking question before spending. The egg list explains what to look for once Snowy is within reach.

subsections.heading: Candy
paragraphs: Candy is the 750,000 Speed gate and the Epic tier. Its pool contains Easter Bunny Egg, Candy Egg and Rainbow Egg. Three listed eggs give you names to compare with the current game, but no hatch odds follow from those names. When considering Candy, first confirm your Speed and then test whether your current Pickaxe handles the eggs comfortably. The shared word “Candy” also appears in the equipment list; that naming overlap does not establish a special unlock relationship between the tool and this zone.

subsections.heading: Swamp
paragraphs: Swamp moves the reference to 12,000,000 Speed and Legendary rarity. Gooey Egg, Tree Egg and Lake Egg are its listed pool. Use the zone gate to judge access and the egg guide to identify the pool; neither table promises an animal's income. At this stage, it is useful to compare the problem you are trying to solve with your next upgrade. If you spend on Power when movement is limiting a run, the higher number on your Pickaxe will not address the Speed requirement.

subsections.heading: Ocean
paragraphs: Ocean requires 150,000,000 Speed. Its Mythic pool contains Sea Stones Egg, Water Egg and Sea Egg. This is the last area in the middle group before Hell. Keep the three egg names distinct when reading lists, since the names refer to entries in the same zone rather than three separate Speed gates. A successful Ocean run still follows the familiar egg-to-base loop. Reaching a higher rarity changes your collection target, but the guide does not assign a hatch chance or Cash rate to that rarity.

subsections.heading: Hell
paragraphs: Hell starts the late group at 1,000,000,000 Speed. Fallen Angel Egg, Angel Egg and Volcanic Egg belong to its Divine pool. The billion-scale gate is worth checking carefully before planning a purchase: 1B in the Speed column describes access, while similarly large numbers in a tool table describe Power or cost. These units cannot be exchanged. If you can reach Hell but spend too long breaking eggs, compare tools. If movement is the issue, review Speed progression and whether your Trail is equipped.

subsections.heading: Blossom
paragraphs: Blossom follows Hell at 5,000,000,000 Speed, with Blossom Egg, Bamboo Egg and Fortune Egg in the Cosmic tier. This is the current step before Galaxy. The egg names identify the pool; “Fortune” does not establish a special payout or a guaranteed result. Keep your planning tied to the stated gate and your own run. You can use Blossom as a collection destination once reachable, while treating any claim about animal income, hidden rewards or hatch odds as a separate question that this table does not answer.

subsections.heading: Galaxy
paragraphs: Galaxy is the highest zone in the current nine-area reference, at 25,000,000,000 Speed. Its Secret pool lists Sun Egg, Starry Egg and Blackhole Egg. That position is the end of the October 8 table, not a claim that every future update will extend the same sequence. The announced New Biome has no published gate or placement yet. For Galaxy itself, check actual Speed rather than a Trail label, and remember that reaching the zone does not remove the need to break an egg and return with its animal.

sections.heading: What to Upgrade When a Zone Feels Too Hard
paragraphs: Match the upgrade to the difficulty you can observe. If you cannot reach the zone or struggle with movement during the return, review Speed and Trails. If an egg takes too long to break after you arrive, review Pickaxe Power. If you want to take more animals per run, the official description identifies bigger satchels as the capacity upgrade.

You do not need a guessed guard statistic or a damage formula to make this distinction. Start with the next reachable zone, complete the loop and compare your next purchase with the part that held you back. For the announced October 11 area, wait for its actual access information rather than treating the next row as automatic.

sections.heading: Egg Rarity Progression
paragraphs: The egg list above groups the current pool by zone. Check the Speed column to see whether the area is reachable, then use the names to identify the eggs you are looking for. The list covers the nine-zone reference as of October 8, 2026; the upcoming New Biome is not assigned an egg pool here.

Rarity is shown alongside each zone's pool. This is a reference for the progression tiers, not a table of hatch probabilities. No animal roster, income value or individual egg break time is implied by a row.

The current rarity order is Common → Uncommon → Rare → Epic → Legendary → Mythic → Divine → Cosmic → Secret. Forest opens the list at Common, while Galaxy closes it at Secret. Reading the order helps you place a zone's eggs in the overall collection route.

Rarity labels do not provide hatch odds. An egg being Mythic or Secret does not tell you the probability of any particular animal, the animal's Cash income or how much Power is required to break it in a fixed time. Use the label to understand the tier and keep those other questions separate.

For collection planning, choose a reachable pool before chasing the highest label. You can see what eggs are associated with your current zone without assuming the late-game pool is practical for your present Speed and tool. The full loop ends with an animal at your base, so access alone is only the start.

sections.heading: How to Choose the Next Egg to Break
paragraphs: Begin with the zone requirement. If your Speed does not meet the area's gate, a stronger Pickaxe will not substitute for entry. Once you can reach the egg, consider whether breaking it is the part that slows the run. Pickaxe Power is the upgrade stat for that task.

After the egg hatches, take the animal and escape the guards. Bringing it to your base and placing it there is what connects the egg choice to earning Cash. A plan that ends at the egg ignores the return, which is a central part of this game's official loop.

Make the next choice around a complete run you can manage. If movement is the problem, review Speed and equipped Trails before assuming another tool solves it. If capacity is the issue, bigger satchels let you take more animals per run. There is no published income comparison here to override those practical checks.

subsections.heading: Forest Eggs
paragraphs: Forest at 5 Speed contains Rock Egg and Forest Egg in the Common tier. This is the starting pool for learning egg breaking, taking an animal and returning to base. Use the two names as a reference for the opening zone, rather than expecting a particular animal from either egg. A first successful return helps you understand what to improve before moving toward Desert.

subsections.heading: Desert Eggs
paragraphs: At 1,000 Speed, Desert introduces Cactus Egg and Bones Egg at Uncommon rarity. Their names distinguish the pool from Forest. Cactus Egg is an egg entry; Cactus also appears as a Pickaxe name elsewhere in the game guide. That overlap does not establish a required equipment pairing. Check entry and breaking performance independently.

subsections.heading: Snowy Eggs
paragraphs: Snowy lists Frozen Egg and Yeti Egg at the 50,000 Speed gate, with Rare rarity. Yeti Egg is the egg name in this reference, not a promise of a specific guaranteed hatch. If you are planning your first visit, compare actual Speed with the gate and then judge your tool through the breaking part of a run.

subsections.heading: Candy Eggs
paragraphs: Candy at 750,000 Speed has Easter Bunny Egg, Candy Egg and Rainbow Egg in the Epic tier. All three belong to the same listed zone pool. A name such as Easter Bunny Egg does not create a separate seasonal event claim in this guide. For progression, the relevant access value remains Candy’s Speed gate.

subsections.heading: Swamp Eggs
paragraphs: Swamp contains Gooey Egg, Tree Egg and Lake Egg at 12,000,000 Speed, with Legendary rarity. This is the tier directly before Mythic. If you are collecting across the pool, use the Index to follow your animal collection while keeping the egg names separate from the animals that hatch.

subsections.heading: Ocean Eggs
paragraphs: Ocean at 150,000,000 Speed lists Sea Stones Egg, Water Egg and Sea Egg as Mythic. The similar names can be easy to mix up, so compare the complete names when checking the pool. The guide does not assign spawn locations within Ocean or claim that one of these eggs has a better income return.

subsections.heading: Hell Eggs
paragraphs: Hell requires 1,000,000,000 Speed and lists Fallen Angel Egg, Angel Egg and Volcanic Egg at Divine rarity. Fallen Angel Egg and Angel Egg are separate names in the same pool. No special boss encounter or guardian statistic is needed to read this list; it supplies the current egg names and access tier.

subsections.heading: Blossom Eggs
paragraphs: Blossom at 5,000,000,000 Speed contains Blossom Egg, Bamboo Egg and Fortune Egg in the Cosmic tier. It is the current step between Hell and Galaxy. Fortune Egg is listed without a reward guarantee or income amount. Use its name to identify the egg, then apply the same breaking and return checks as for other pools.

subsections.heading: Galaxy Eggs
paragraphs: Galaxy’s Sun Egg, Starry Egg and Blackhole Egg sit in the Secret tier at 25,000,000,000 Speed. This is the highest pool in the current reference. It does not tell us what eggs will appear in the announced New Biome, or whether a new area will follow Galaxy in the same order.

sections.heading: Eggs, Animals and the Index
paragraphs: Eggs hatch animals; those animals are what you take away from the guards and place in your base to earn Cash. The egg list therefore describes the source pool, not a complete list of the creatures you will collect. The official game description also mentions an Index for collection.

Use that distinction when checking progress. Finding an egg name in this table is different from filling an animal entry in the Index. This guide does not publish an animal roster, hatch percentages, weights or earnings that have not been established for the current game.

For the next update, check the separate event page. The announcement confirms a new area, but its eggs and animals have not been announced as of this guide's date. Continue using the current pool for present progression and return to the main wiki when you need the wider route.

title: Break and Steal an Egg Pickaxes Guide
description: Compare all 18 Break and Steal an Egg pickaxes, costs and Power values, plus when to upgrade your tool instead of spending on Speed or Trails.

hero.heading: Break and Steal an Egg Pickaxes
hero.lead: The current reference lists 18 Pickaxes, from Wooden through Celestial. Their Power helps break eggs faster and is separate from Speed. If breaking is slow, compare tools below; for movement or zone access, review Speed and Trails.

sections.heading: All Break and Steal an Egg Pickaxes
What Pickaxe Power Does
paragraphs: The current Pickaxe list contains 18 tools, from the starter Wooden Pickaxe to Celestial. Compare cost and Power side by side before planning an upgrade. The list is the October 8, 2026 reference and does not assign an egg requirement, rarity or damage formula to a tool.

Cost is a purchase value; Power is the stat used for egg breaking. Keep those columns separate from Speed gates in the zone guide. Short labels such as K, M, B and T indicate the scale of the listed values. Qa is retained as displayed in the late-game cost reference, so you can compare it with the game's own labels.

Pickaxe Power helps you break eggs more efficiently. It addresses the part of the run before you take the hatched animal. If you can already reach a zone but spend too long at an egg, checking a stronger tool is a sensible next step.

Power does not serve as Speed for zone access or movement. A tool with a large Power value may still leave your access problem unresolved if the zone gate is above your actual Speed. Likewise, buying a Trail does not replace the Pickaxe stat used to break an egg.

This table does not support a precise time-to-break calculation. That would need egg health and the game's damage rules, which are not supplied here. Compare the listed tools and your actual run instead of treating a Power ratio as a guaranteed timer. No exact number of hits is promised for any egg.

links.label: Check eggs in your reachable zone

sections.heading: Early Pickaxe Progression
paragraphs: The opening order is Wooden → Stone → Iron → Golden. Wooden is the starter at 1 Power. Stone costs $80 for 4 Power and Iron costs $800 for 15 Power. These are the first listed purchase steps after the starting tool.

Golden raises the reference to 60 Power at $20K. Compare both columns before buying: a larger Power number does not address a Speed gate, and a tool purchase should fit the part of the run you are trying to improve. Diamond begins the next group in this guide.

During your first sessions, learn whether egg breaking is actually your main limit. If movement or zone access is holding you back, saving only for a Pickaxe does not directly solve that issue. The beginner route helps you make a complete run first, then choose between Power, Speed and carrying capacity based on what happened.

sections.heading: Mid-Game Pickaxes
paragraphs: The middle group runs Diamond → Strawberry → Cactus → Lightning → Candy → Rainbow → Crystal. Diamond costs $160K for 250 Power. Strawberry follows at $1.2M and 1K Power; Cactus at $6M and 4K Power; and Lightning at $40M and 15K Power.

Candy reaches 60K Power at $400M, Rainbow reaches 250K at $2.8B, and Crystal reaches 1M at $20B. These names are tool entries. A matching word in an egg or zone name does not establish a required pairing: Candy Pickaxe is not listed here as a special key for Candy zone.

At this stage, compare the next tool with how the breaking part of your current run feels. You do not need to buy a named tool just because a guide mentions a zone with a similar theme. Start with the relevant stat and avoid spending around an unannounced egg-health threshold or a claimed guaranteed return.

sections.heading: Late-Game Pickaxes
paragraphs: The late group is Demon → Hacker → UFO → Secret → Cool → Galaxy → Celestial. Demon costs $120B for 4M Power, Hacker $1.2T for 15M, and UFO $12T for 60M. Secret follows at $80T with 250M Power.

Cool is listed at $600T and 1B Power. Galaxy costs $4Qa for 5B Power, and Celestial is the strongest entry in this reference at $20Qa and 25B Power. “Strongest listed” describes the largest Power value in this table; it does not establish the best purchase for every player's current bottleneck.

Large equipment values do not remove the separate Speed requirement for a zone. Galaxy Pickaxe and Galaxy zone also use different columns and different kinds of values. Check the tool's Power for breaking and the zone's gate for entry. The upcoming New Biome has no published tool requirement to add to this comparison.

sections.heading: Pickaxe or Trail — What Should You Buy Next?
paragraphs: Think about the last run you attempted. Which part took too long or stopped you? The decision table points to the stat worth checking next, without promising a fixed purchase order for every account. Your current equipment and reachable zone matter more than choosing the most expensive name on either list.

If you decide to buy a Trail, remember to equip it so the multiplier applies. If you choose a Pickaxe, judge the result at the egg-breaking stage of a comparable run. Keeping those observations separate makes it easier to see whether the upgrade addressed the actual problem.

There is no income or return-on-investment formula in this guide. The official Cash loop depends on bringing animals back and placing them at your base, so a decision should consider whether you can complete the run as well as whether the egg breaks faster.

faq.answer: Wooden is the starter Pickaxe. It is listed with 1 Power and no purchase cost beyond the Starter label.

faq.answer: Celestial has the highest listed Power at 25B, with a reference cost of $20Qa. That does not make it the necessary next purchase for every player.

faq.answer: No. The zone reference uses Speed gates. Power helps you break eggs once you can reach them.

faq.question: Should I buy a Pickaxe or Trail first?
faq.answer: Check your bottleneck. If breaking is slow, look at Pickaxe Power. If movement or zone access is limiting you, review Speed and equipped Trails.

faq.question: What is the first paid pickaxe?
faq.answer: Stone is the first paid Pickaxe in the current list, at $80 with 4 Power. Wooden is the starter tool at 1 Power.

faq.answer: No. Power helps break eggs faster. Speed and equipped Trail multipliers belong to movement and zone progression.

title: Break and Steal an Egg Trails & Speed Guide
description: Compare Break and Steal an Egg trails, costs and Speed multipliers, learn how equipping works, and choose the next trail for your progression.

hero.heading: Break and Steal an Egg Trails
hero.lead: The current reference lists 11 Trails, from White at 2x through Moonlight at 10Kx. Buying a Trail is not enough: equip it for the Speed multiplier to apply. Trails help Speed progression; Pickaxes provide Power for egg breaking.

sections.heading: All Break and Steal an Egg Trails

table.caption: Current Trails — equip to apply the multiplier

sections.callout: Equip the Trail after buying it. Ownership alone does not apply the multiplier.

sections.heading: How Trails Work
paragraphs: The current Trail list has 11 entries, from White at 2x to Moonlight at 10Kx. Use the cost and multiplier columns together when comparing the next purchase. These values are the October 8, 2026 reference; no higher tier or hidden training formula is added.

A multiplier describes the Trail's listed Speed benefit when equipped. It is not the same as your actual Speed, and it is not a zone gate. For example, Galaxy's gate is 25,000,000,000 Speed, while the Trail table contains multipliers and Cash costs. Matching a number across those columns would mix different measurements.

Trails provide the Speed multiplier system, and the equip step matters. If you have purchased a Trail but have not equipped it, its listed multiplier is not applied. Check your equipped setup before concluding that the purchase has failed to help your progression.

Speed is the part of your setup associated with movement and zone access. Pickaxe Power belongs to egg breaking. A Trail is therefore a different kind of upgrade from a tool, even when both are bought with Cash. Decide which stat needs attention before comparing the largest available values.

For training, use the instructions and Speed display in the game. This guide does not calculate treadmill gains, training time or final Speed from a hidden formula. Players may start from different values, so the same Trail does not mean the same zone access for everyone. Check actual progress after equipping rather than relying on a name or an assumed conversion.

sections.heading: Trail Progression from White to Moonlight

subsections.heading: Early Trails
paragraphs: White begins at $500 with a 2x multiplier. Blue follows at $7.5K and 4x, Green at $100K and 8x, and Purple at $1.2M and 16x. The early sequence gives you clear comparison points as you learn Speed progression.

Before saving for the next entry, confirm that your current Trail is equipped. Then consider whether Speed is the part slowing your run or whether breaking needs more Power. Buying a new Trail while leaving the previous one unequipped can obscure the difference between the two purchases.

subsections.heading: Mid-Game Trails
paragraphs: Red costs $17.5M for 40x, Golden costs $250M for 100x, and Rainbow costs $3.5B for 250x. The costs grow alongside the multipliers, so read both columns before planning a purchase. A bigger multiplier is useful to compare, but the table does not supply a guaranteed training duration.

These are Trail names, not egg rarity labels. Rainbow also appears in egg and Pickaxe names, without establishing a special combination or requirement. Use the Speed role of the Trail to decide whether it fits the difficulty you are trying to solve.

subsections.heading: Late Trails
paragraphs: Galactic is listed at $45B and 600x. Secret follows at $600B and 1.5Kx, Laser at $8T and 4Kx, and Moonlight at $100T and 10Kx. Moonlight is the highest multiplier in the current list, equivalent to the listed 10,000x label.

The late Trail sequence does not provide a guaranteed unlock route for Galaxy or the future New Biome. Your actual Speed remains the number to compare with any announced gate. An expensive Trail can be a progression purchase without being proof that a particular destination is immediately reachable.

sections.heading: Trails vs. Pickaxes
paragraphs: Compare systems by the task they affect. A Trail helps with Speed progression; a Pickaxe helps with Power for egg breaking. Both belong to the larger earning loop, but buying one does not give you the other stat's function.

If you arrive at an egg comfortably and breaking is slow, the Pickaxe list is the more relevant next reference. If you break it but movement makes reaching the area or returning difficult, review Speed and your equipped Trail. If you want to carry more animals, the official description points to bigger satchels instead.

There is no single purchase order that follows from these tables for every player. Identify the bottleneck, check what is equipped and choose a purchase that targets it. The beginner guide walks through that decision after a full return to base.

table.caption: Trail or Pickaxe: match the stat to the task

sections.heading: Trails and Zone Speed
paragraphs: Zone access should be checked against your Speed display. The current route starts at Forest with 5 Speed, then moves through progressively larger gates to Galaxy at 25B. The complete zone guide lists each threshold and its egg pool.

Do not turn this route into a guaranteed Trail-to-zone chart. Because actual Speed differs between players, a named Trail alone does not establish that you can enter a particular zone. Equip your Trail, use the game's training system and compare the resulting stat with the gate you want to reach.

For the scheduled New Biome, no Speed requirement has been announced. There is no specific Trail to recommend as its access key. Continue current progression and read the new area's announced requirements when available, rather than spending toward a guessed threshold.

faq.answer: Trails provide Speed multipliers for progression. They are separate from the Power stat provided by Pickaxes.

faq.answer: Yes. Buying it is not enough; the Trail must be equipped for its listed multiplier to apply.

faq.answer: White is the first listed Trail, with a 2x multiplier and a $500 reference cost.

faq.answer: Moonlight has the highest listed multiplier at 10Kx, with a reference cost of $100T.

faq.question: Are Trails the same as Pickaxes?
faq.answer: No. Trails help Speed progression, while Pickaxe Power helps break eggs. Choose between them by the task slowing your run.

faq.question: Which Trail do I need for Galaxy?
faq.answer: There is no guaranteed Trail choice from the table alone. Galaxy requires 25,000,000,000 actual Speed; access depends on your own Speed progression and equipped setup.

faq.answer: The current guide lists 11 Trails, from White through Moonlight, with their reference Cash costs and Speed multipliers.

faq.answer: First check that the purchased Trail is equipped: ownership alone does not apply its multiplier. Use the actual Speed display to judge progression; this guide does not assume a hidden training formula.

title: Break and Steal an Egg Beginner Guide
description: Learn how to play Break and Steal an Egg: train Speed, break eggs, steal animals, escape guards, earn Cash, and choose your first upgrades.

hero.heading: Break and Steal an Egg Beginner Guide
hero.lead: Train enough Speed for a reachable zone, equip your Pickaxe, break an egg and take the hatched animal. Escape the guards, place the animal at your base for Cash and upgrade the part slowing your run. This route is for ILGames x Eggs on Roblox, Place ID 114326934417838.

sections.heading: Your First Break and Steal an Egg Run
paragraphs: Break and Steal an Egg turns an egg into a base-earning animal through a complete run. The first session is easiest to understand when you follow that whole sequence once, instead of treating training, tools and collection as unrelated tasks.

This route is for the ILGames x Eggs experience on Roblox, Place ID 114326934417838. Check that destination before using a guide for a similarly named game. You do not need a redeem code to learn the loop, and this walkthrough does not assume an unannounced free reward.

steps.heading: Find your base and current Speed
steps.description: Begin by locating your base and reading your current Speed. The run will end back at the base, so know your return destination before setting out. Speed is the number to compare with zone access, not your Cash balance or Pickaxe Power.

steps.heading: Train for the first reachable zone
steps.description: Use Speed training to reach your first area. The current Forest reference gate is 5 Speed. Check the value shown in the game before planning a visit, and do not assume a stronger tool replaces this requirement.

steps.heading: Equip the Wooden Pickaxe and break a Forest egg
steps.description: The Wooden Pickaxe is the starter tool at 1 Power. Forest lists Rock Egg and Forest Egg in the Common tier. Equip your tool and use it to break an egg. Notice whether this part of the run is what takes the longest.

steps.heading: Take the animal after it hatches
steps.description: Eggs hatch animals. Take the animal to continue the earning loop; breaking the egg alone is not the final goal. Bigger satchels allow more animals per run, but learn the basic take-and-return route before planning around carrying more.

steps.heading: Escape the guards and return to your base
steps.description: Bring the animal back while escaping the guards. Pay attention to the movement part of the run so you can tell whether Speed is the next thing to improve. This guide does not assume a particular guard statistic or a fixed escape time.

steps.heading: Place the animal to start earning Cash
steps.description: Place the animal at your base to earn Cash, as described in the official game loop. This connects the egg-breaking and return stages to progression. No fixed earnings amount is needed to understand why finishing the run matters.

steps.heading: Use the next purchase to fix the actual bottleneck
steps.description: Review what slowed the run. Look at Pickaxe Power for breaking, Speed and equipped Trails for movement, or satchel capacity for taking more animals. Choose the relevant system before comparing its next purchase, then judge the result on another complete run.

sections.heading: What Each Upgrade Solves
paragraphs: The main systems address different parts of progression. Use the table as a quick way to decide which guide to open after a run. Some systems have cost tables in this wiki; satchels and the Index are described only at the high level confirmed by the official game description.

A purchase should solve an observed problem. If an egg is slow to break, a carrying upgrade will not directly speed that stage up. If you want to take more animals per trip, a stronger Pickaxe does not by itself increase satchel capacity. Keeping the roles clear makes the first upgrade decision much easier.

sections.heading: Speed vs. Pickaxe Power
paragraphs: Speed and Power are separate checks. Speed determines whether your progression meets a zone's listed access gate and belongs to the movement side of a run. Pickaxe Power is the tool stat for egg breaking once you can reach an egg.

A Trail helps Speed progression, but only when equipped. If you buy one, check the equipped setup before expecting its multiplier. The Pickaxe guide instead compares tools by cost and Power; it does not promise a precise number of hits for each egg.

When deciding what to buy first, describe the problem in one sentence: “I cannot reach the zone,” “the egg takes too long,” or “I want to carry more animals.” Then match that sentence to the appropriate system. There is no universal budget split in this guide, because your current stat values and the part limiting your run can differ.

sections.heading: Your First Zones
paragraphs: Forest is the opening reference at 5 Speed, with Rock Egg and Forest Egg in the Common tier. Desert follows at 1,000 Speed with Cactus Egg and Bones Egg at Uncommon. Snowy is the next early destination at 50,000 Speed, listing Frozen Egg and Yeti Egg at Rare.

Treat those gates as access targets, then evaluate the whole run in each area. Reaching a new rarity tier is different from being comfortable with breaking and bringing an animal back. You can improve the part that slows you down before planning a longer progression jump.

The full zone table continues through Candy, Swamp, Ocean, Hell, Blossom and Galaxy. You do not need that entire late-game route memorized for the first session. Use the current next gate and its egg pool as a focused goal, then return to the larger reference when you are ready.

links.label: Find eggs by zone and rarity

subsections.heading: Following the wrong egg game
paragraphs: Steal An Egg is a different Roblox experience. Match the developer ILGames x Eggs and Place ID 114326934417838 when checking guides or code claims. A similar name does not make another game’s rewards, menus or progression values applicable here.

subsections.heading: Spending on the wrong bottleneck
paragraphs: Choose the stat that addresses the part slowing the run. Power is relevant to egg breaking; Speed matters for access and movement. Review a complete attempt before choosing a purchase from the tool or Trail table simply because its number is larger.

subsections.heading: Buying a Trail without equipping it
paragraphs: The listed multiplier requires the Trail to be equipped. Check this step before buying another upgrade to solve a Speed issue. Ownership and the active equipped setup are different things, and the latter is what matters for the multiplier.

subsections.heading: Chasing rarity before finishing a return
paragraphs: Higher rarity pools are progression targets, but an egg is only the beginning of the earning route. Practice taking the animal and placing it at your base. This advice does not assume a particular failure penalty; it follows the official loop from egg to Cash.

sections.heading: What to Read Next
paragraphs: Choose the next guide by the question you have now. Codes covers the current confirmed code status and the separate community reward offer. Zones gives the next Speed gate, while Eggs identifies the pool once you know your destination. Pickaxes and Trails help you compare purchases for different stats.

For the next announced update, New Biome contains the October 11 event schedule and the details known as of October 8. No future zone requirement is needed for this beginner route. The main wiki brings these pages together when you want to switch from a focused question to the overall progression picture.

faq.question: How do you play Break and Steal an Egg?
faq.answer: Reach a zone, break an egg, take the animal, escape guards and place the animal at your base for Cash. Use upgrades to improve the part that slows the run.

faq.question: What should I upgrade first?
faq.answer: Fix the bottleneck you observe. Check Power if breaking is slow, Speed or equipped Trails for movement, and satchels if you want more carrying capacity.

faq.question: What is Speed used for?
faq.answer: Speed belongs to movement and progression through zone access gates. Forest starts the current reference at 5 Speed.

faq.question: What does Pickaxe Power do?
faq.answer: It helps break eggs faster. It does not replace the Speed required to enter a zone.

faq.question: How do Trails work?
faq.answer: Trails provide Speed multipliers. A purchased Trail must be equipped before its multiplier applies.

faq.question: What is the first zone?
faq.answer: Forest is the first listed zone at 5 Speed, containing Rock Egg and Forest Egg at Common rarity.

faq.question: Are there any codes for beginners?
faq.answer: There are no confirmed working redeem codes as of October 8, 2026. The official like-and-group reward offer is separate from codes.
